sentences.en: I saw Trump won, figured it would be a bit.
sentences.zh: 我看到特朗普赢了，还以为会是一场恶战。

sentences.en: Now the pressure really starts to finish that mid-year examination of Hillary Clinton, meaning that Clinton didn't approve.
sentences.zh: 现在压力真的开始增大，要完成对希拉里·克林顿年中审查的收尾工作，这意味着克林顿并未批准。

sentences.en: They worry about the effect he's going to have on the
sentences.zh: 他们担心他将对

sentences.en: FBI.
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局产生的影响。

sentences.en: They complain about the way he treats minorities.
sentences.zh: 他们抱怨他对待少数族裔的方式。

sentences.en: They say he's a bully.
sentences.zh: 他们说他是个霸凌者。

sentences.en: And earlier in February 2016, Page texted struck that candidate Trump simply cannot be president.
sentences.zh: 早在2016年2月，佩奇就给斯特佐克发短信说，候选人特朗普绝对不能当总统。

sentences.en: And all of this is in text messages.
sentences.zh: 而所有这些都记录在短信中。

sentences.en: I feel like we've already heard about these two agents.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们已经听过这两个特工的事了。

sentences.en: Trump has focused on them for months as kind of perfect representatives of political bias within the FBI.
sentences.zh: 特朗普几个月来一直盯着他们，把他们当作FBI内部政治偏见的完美代表。

sentences.en: Is there anything new in this report about them?
sentences.zh: 这份报告里关于他们有什么新鲜内容吗？

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: And it's potentially one of the more damaging revelations of the report.
sentences.zh: 这可能是这份报告中最具杀伤力的爆料之一。

sentences.en: On August 8th, 2016, one FBI official, a lawyer by the name of Lisa Page, is talking about Trump and says, oh, he's not going to be president, is he?
sentences.zh: 2016年8月8日，一名FBI官员，一位名叫丽莎·佩吉的律师，在谈到特朗普时说，哦，他不会成为总统的，对吧？

sentences.en: The other, Pete Strzok, says, no, no, he's not.
sentences.zh: 另一位皮特·斯特佐克说，不，不，他不会的。

sentences.en: We'll stop it.
sentences.zh: 我们会阻止他的。

sentences.en: And so that will stop it if you're President Trump or you're one of his supporters or, frankly, if you're anybody just reading these cold.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是特朗普总统，或者你是他的支持者，或者坦率地说，如果你只是任何一个字面阅读这些内容的人，这就会阻止他。

sentences.en: It looks like, well, there was bias at the heart of the FBI.
sentences.zh: 看起来，嗯，FBI的核心存在偏见。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That seems to very much support how President Trump talks about the FBI.
sentences.zh: 这似乎非常印证了特朗普总统对FBI的说法。

sentences.en: It absolutely does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I've read all of the text messages that have been released publicly.
sentences.zh: 我读过所有公开发布的短信。

sentences.en: There's no question that this is the one that most clearly backs up President Trump's theory that the FBI or that key people at the FBI were out to stop him.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这是最清楚地支持特朗普总统理论的一条，即FBI或FBI的关键人物当时正千方百计阻止他。

sentences.en: So how could that message be part of this report and yet the overall conclusion of this report
sentences.zh: 那么，这条信息怎么会成为这份报告的一部分，而这份报告的总体结论却是

sentences.en: be that bias was not really the issue and that this was about insubordination and dysfunction?
sentences.zh: 偏见其实不是问题，这关乎抗命不尊和职能失调？

sentences.en: What the inspector general said was these text messages were really bad and they created the
sentences.zh: 总检察长所说的是，这些短信非常糟糕，它们造成了

sentences.en: impression of bias and they sowed doubt and they undermined the confidence in the investigation,
sentences.zh: 偏见的印象，播下了怀疑的种子，并削弱了人们对调查的信心，

sentences.en: but that they weren't able to find any evidence of an actual investigative step that any of these agents took that was based on bias.
sentences.zh: 但他们未能找到任何证据表明这些特工采取了基于偏见的实际调查行动。

sentences.en: So FBI officials are actually allowed to have their own political beliefs.
sentences.zh: 所以FBI官员其实是被允许拥有自己的政治信仰的。

sentences.en: They are actually also allowed to express political beliefs, but they're not allowed to let their views influence their investigative decisions.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上也被允许表达政治信仰，但他们不能让自己的观点影响调查决定。

sentences.en: And what the inspector general said was, we don't have evidence that their political views influence the decisions.
sentences.zh: 总检察长说的是，我们没有证据表明他们的政治观点影响了这些决定。

sentences.en: And then there's the reality, right, that the FBI's decisions weren't helpful to Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一个现实，对吧，那就是FBI的决定对希拉里·克林顿并没有什么帮助。

sentences.en: And so getting a unified theory of the case is very difficult because there are a lot of different strands here.
sentences.zh: 因此，要对这起案件形成一个统一的理论非常困难，因为这里有许多不同的线索。

sentences.en: It's just, it's complicated.
sentences.zh: 这只是，这很复杂。

sentences.en: It doesn't, it doesn't all fit neatly together.
sentences.zh: 它并不，它并不能完全天衣无缝地拼凑在一起。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so much of what's been happening in the United States over the past year or so since this election has been about perception and about spin on both sides.
sentences.zh: 过去一年左右，自从这次选举以来，美国发生的大量事情都与双方的感知和舆论引导有关。

sentences.en: So even if those texts didn't affect the outcome of the election, according to this IG report, doesn't the fact that this report
sentences.zh: 所以，即使这些短信没有影响选举结果，根据这份IG报告，难道这份报告

sentences.en: shows us that messages like that were present inside the FBI, isn't that what matters?
sentences.zh: 向我们展示了FBI内部存在这样的信息，这难道不才是最重要的吗？

sentences.en: I think that is what matters.
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是最重要的。

sentences.en: I think the FBI has a brand and the brand is we don't do politics.
sentences.zh: 我认为FBI有一个品牌，这个品牌就是我们不搞政治。

sentences.en: And whether you're a Democrat or Republican, you need to be able to believe in that.
sentences.zh: 无论你是民主党人还是共和党人，你都需要能够相信这一点。

sentences.en: And while on the one hand, the report today doesn't undermine that because it says there's
sentences.zh: 一方面，今天的报告并没有动摇这一点，因为它说没有

sentences.en: no evidence that bias steered the outcome, it really just lays bare a lot of dysfunction and
sentences.zh: 证据表明偏见左右了结果，但它确实彻底暴露了大量的职能失调和

sentences.en: embarrassing stuff that is just going to make people question the credibility of the FBI.
sentences.zh: 令人尴尬的事情，这些只会让人们质疑FBI的信誉。

sentences.en: And that's not good for, that is not good for the brand.
sentences.zh: 这对于，这对这个品牌来说不是什么好事。

sentences.en: And it's not good for the country.
sentences.zh: 这对国家也不是好事。

sentences.en: So going back to that op-ed that James Comey just wrote for The Times, he says that this report is good for the FBI.
sentences.zh: 所以回到詹姆斯·科米刚刚为《时报》写的专栏文章，他说这份报告对FBI有好处。

sentences.en: It doesn't sound like you think this report is good for the FBI.
sentences.zh: 听起来你并不认为这份报告对FBI有好处。

sentences.en: Well, it certainly could have been worse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它当然可能会更糟。

sentences.en: I mean, if the inspector general had come out and found
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果总检察长出来发现

sentences.en: that political biases steered the outcome of a criminal investigation, I mean, that would have been catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 政治偏见左右了一项刑事调查的结果，我的意思是，那将是灾难性的。

sentences.en: So no, it's not a good day.
sentences.zh: 所以不，这不是个好日子。

sentences.en: But I mean, yeah, it could it certainly could have been much worse.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，是的，它当然可能会糟得多。

sentences.en: Well, I wonder if one of the most important things is this, to your point, we have been talking about
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想其中最重要的事情之一是这个，正如你所说，我们一直在讨论

sentences.en: the fact that this investigation was not directly about the Russia investigation or the special counsel, Robert Mueller.
sentences.zh: 这样一个事实，即这次调查并非直接关于俄罗斯调查或特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒。

sentences.en: But I wonder if in this climate, and given how the president talks about all this, if this inspector general report inevitably becomes part of the Russia investigation, because
sentences.zh: 但我想在这种氛围下，考虑到总统对这一切的言论，这份总检察长报告是否不可避免地成为了俄罗斯调查的一部分，因为

sentences.en: Comey's now a vocal critic of Trump and a key witness in the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 科米现在是特朗普的公开批评者，也是俄罗斯调查的关键证人。

sentences.en: And these FBI agents were involved in both of those investigations, Clinton and Trump.
sentences.zh: 而这些FBI特工都卷入了这两项调查，克林顿和特朗普。

sentences.en: So doesn't this report inevitably become part of the special counsel investigation?
sentences.zh: 所以这份报告难道不会不可避免地成为特别检察官调查的一部分吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's funny, I don't I don't think it will.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，我不认为，我不认为会。

sentences.en: I think when Robert Mueller, the special counsel took over this investigation, you know, he brought in a dozen prosecutors and he has his own agents.
sentences.zh: 我认为当特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒接管这项调查时，你知道，他带进来一打检察官，他有自己的特工。

sentences.en: And I don't think the origins of it are going to necessarily steer the outcome of it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它的起源一定会左右它的结果。

sentences.en: And I think Mueller will probably rise and fall on the credibility of whatever he brings or doesn't bring.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为穆勒最终的成败将取决于他带来的或没有带来的证据的可信度。

sentences.en: But I think what is at issue here is now when President Trump says, don't believe the FBI,
sentences.zh: 但我想现在的问题是，当特朗普总统说，不要相信FBI时，

sentences.en: are people going to read this report and say, hey, you know, he's got a point?
sentences.zh: 人们会读这份报告然后说，嘿，你知道，他说的有道理吗？

sentences.en: Or are they going to read all 500 pages and see that, well, no, it's not that simple?
sentences.zh: 还是他们会读完所有的500页，然后发现，嗯，不，事情没那么简单？

sentences.en: Or are they just going to go to the part that says Comey's insubordinate and, you know, this guy didn't like Trump and these rules weren't followed.
sentences.zh: 或者他们只会去看那部分，说科米抗命不尊，然后，你知道，这家伙不喜欢特朗普，这些规则没有被遵守。

sentences.en: And I think that's how this matters to the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是这对俄罗斯调查重要的地方。

sentences.en: It matters to, like, what do people think of the FBI?
sentences.zh: 它关乎，比如，人们怎么看FBI？

sentences.en: And if ultimately the Russia case is resolved in a political way, whether it's an impeachment hearing or at the polls, that's where I think people's impressions
sentences.zh: 如果最终俄罗斯案件以一种政治方式解决，无论是弹劾听证会还是通过投票，我认为这才是人们对FBI的印象

sentences.en: of the FBI are going to matter.
sentences.zh: 将会发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: Well, I heard a theory today that because this report seems to support elements of the
sentences.zh: 嗯，我今天听到一种理论，因为这份报告似乎支持了

sentences.en: president's argument for firing James Comey and is so critical of Comey and his behavior in office
sentences.zh: 总统解雇詹姆斯·科米的论点的部分内容，并且对科米及其在任期间的行为极其批评，

sentences.en: that it would undermine a case of obstruction of justice by President Trump, which is a huge part of the special counsel's probe.
sentences.zh: 以至于它会削弱特朗普总统妨碍司法公正的罪名，而这是特别检察官调查的巨大一部分。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Nobody argues that the president had the authority to fire Jim Comey.
sentences.zh: 没有人争论总统是否有权解雇吉姆·科米。

sentences.en: And nobody argues that he had authority to fire Jim Comey because he handled the Clinton investigation in ways the president thought was inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 也没有人争论他是否有权解雇吉姆·科米，因为他处理克林顿调查的方式被总统认为是不合适的。

sentences.en: Done.
sentences.zh: 结束了。

sentences.en: Over.
sentences.zh: 完了。

sentences.en: That is settled.
sentences.zh: 这已经定论了。

sentences.en: What the issue is is, yeah, but is that really what happened?
sentences.zh: 问题是，是的，但那真的是发生的事情吗？

sentences.en: Like, did he really do that?
sentences.zh: 比如，他真的那样做了吗？

sentences.en: And so today's report comes out and says there were plenty of problems at the FBI.
sentences.zh: 所以今天的报告出来说，FBI存在大量问题。

sentences.en: And so if President Trump really did fire Jim Comey because of the Clinton investigation, then yeah, I think this is fine.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果特朗普总统真的因为克林顿调查而解雇了吉姆·科米，那么是的，我认为这没问题。

sentences.en: This report, I guess, is another thing he can point to.
sentences.zh: 我想这份报告是另一个他可以指出的点。

sentences.en: Not that he needs it.
sentences.zh: 倒不是他需要这个。

sentences.en: But Mueller's not investigating that.
sentences.zh: 但穆勒调查的不是那个。

sentences.en: Mueller's investigating did he fire Jim Comey because he was secretly trying to, you know, protect himself and corruptly trying to protect his buddies in the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 穆勒调查的是他解雇吉姆·科米是不是因为他暗中试图，你知道，保护自己，并腐败地试图保护他在俄罗斯调查中的铁哥们。

sentences.en: And this report doesn't weigh in on that at all.
sentences.zh: 而这份报告根本没有对这一点进行权衡。

sentences.en: But Matt, does this report undermine Comey's credibility as a witness in the Russia investigation,
sentences.zh: 但是，马特，这份报告难道没有削弱科米作为俄罗斯调查证人的可信度吗，

sentences.en: especially as such a unique witness who is often alone with the president in rooms where things were said that could determine the outcome of the investigation?
sentences.zh: 特别作为这样一个独特的证人，他经常独自与总统呆在房间里，在那里说出的话可能会决定调查的结果？

sentences.en: I think your views on Jim Comey, if you have them, are pretty much locked in at this point.
sentences.zh: 我认为你对吉姆·科米的看法，如果你有的话，在这个阶段基本上已经定型了。

sentences.en: I mean, the report was not certainly not flattering to Comey, but it didn't bring a lot of new information to light on him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这份报告当然对科米很不客气，但它并没有带来多少关于他的新信息。

sentences.en: And if you think that Comey made difficult choices in a difficult time but did them for noble reasons, this report's not going to change that.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为科米在艰难的时期做出了艰难的选择，但他是为了崇高的原因而做的，这份报告不会改变这一点。

sentences.en: And if you think that Jim
sentences.zh: 如果你认为吉姆·

sentences.en: Comey is an arrogant, go-it-alone guy who took it upon himself to make decisions that he shouldn't have been making, then this report's not going to change that either.
sentences.zh: 科米是一个傲慢的、独断专行的人，他擅自做决定，做他本不该做的决定，那么这份报告也不会改变这一点。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, this report is basically supporting everyone's view of everything, as it already was.
sentences.zh: 所以，这份报告基本上是在印证每个人对一切事情的固有看法。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不对。

sentences.en: Depending on what you're looking for in this report, you can probably find evidence to support your views.
sentences.zh: 根据你在寻找什么，你可能在这份报告中找到支持你观点的证据。

sentences.en: But I do think, just as a historical document, I think it's important.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，仅作为一个历史文献，我认为它很重要。

sentences.en: I think it's worth reading all 500 pages and trying to read it with an open mind and without coming to it with
sentences.zh: 我认为值得通读全部500页，并试着以开放的心态去读，不要带着

sentences.en: those views, because it is a fascinating look at the FBI in the most chaotic, politically significant moment in its modern history.
sentences.zh: 那些观点去读，因为它对FBI在其现代史上最混乱、最具政治意义的时刻进行了迷人的审视。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.

sentences.en: Until this summer.

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
